Track variant frequency trajectories over time

Source: R/longitudinal.R
trackFrequency.Rd

Extracts per-variant allele frequency trajectories across longitudinal time points within each host. Returns a long-format DataFrame suitable for downstream analysis or plotting.

Usage

trackFrequency(
  whe,
  hostCol = "host_id",
  timeCol = "timepoint",
  usePassedOnly = TRUE
)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment with longitudinal samples from the same host.

hostCol

Character scalar. Column name in colData containing the host/patient identifier (default: "host_id").

timeCol

Character scalar. Column name in colData containing the time point (default: "timepoint"). It must hold numbers, dates, date-times, time differences or a factor whose levels are in time order; text is read as numbers when every value is one, and is otherwise an error, as in flagTemporalInconsistency. Samples whose time point is NA are left out, with a warning.

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default), only use variants where qcPass == TRUE. With FALSE every call is returned and qc_passed marks those that failed.

Value

A DataFrame with columns:

host_id

Host identifier.

variant_key

Unique variant identifier (chrom:pos:alt).

timepoint

Time point value.

frequency

Alternative allele frequency at that time point.

qc_passed

Logical. Whether the call passed QC at that time point; an NA qcPass counts as not passed (TRUE if no QC assay present).

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(100, 200), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("A", "C")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("T", "G")
freq <- matrix(c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20), nrow = 2, ncol = 2)
whe <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = freq),
    rowRanges = gr,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("S1_t1", "S1_t2"),
        host_id = c("H1", "H1"),
        timepoint = c(1, 2)))
trackFrequency(whe)
#> DataFrame with 4 rows and 5 columns
#>       host_id variant_key timepoint frequency qc_passed
#>   <character> <character> <numeric> <numeric> <logical>
#> 1          H1  seg1:100:T         1      0.05      TRUE
#> 2          H1  seg1:200:G         1      0.10      TRUE
#> 3          H1  seg1:100:T         2      0.15      TRUE
#> 4          H1  seg1:200:G         2      0.20      TRUE
